chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Zurara ibn Ayn, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
There is no problem if there happen to be the resemblances in the houses when its heads are changed from it and it is left, what is besides that.

key_terms.التَّمَاثِيلُ: Statues or images of living beings

ai.seo_question: Are statues allowed in Shia Islam if their heads are removed?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the Shia juristic position on *taswir* (image-making), distinguishing between full idols and decorative figures by permitting statues in homes if their heads are altered to prevent full veneration. This ruling reflects the scholarly consensus that the prohibition primarily targets images intended for worship or those possessing complete human-like features, thereby allowing for artistic expression in domestic settings. It highlights the practical application of the principle of *istihlak* (consumption of the prohibition) through partial modification.
